h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבָּת תְּשׁוּבָה, י״ז Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 17

p: It is stated in the Pesikta
All the prophets call Yisrael to teshuvah,
and they do not teach Yisrael
and teaches them with what they should appease Him, etc.:
וּבִפְסִיקְתָּא הַחֲדָשָׁה (פְּסִיקְתָּא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא כד, יח):
And in the Pesikta Chadashah (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana 24:18):
Was it not with words that you beguiled Him at Sinai?
and with their tongue they lied to Him"
This is along the lines of what Chazal said
and said to him, "What became of your judgment?"
He said to him, "I did teshuvah and reached a compromise."
saying, "Such is the power of teshuvah,
"A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day:
it is good to give thanks to Hashem"
that they expounded from the word "va'ochel"
that he said, "I ate, and I will eat again."
the magnitude of the damage he had done;
only, because he knew of himself
he had given the yetzer hara dominion over his soul,
it was over this that he lamented,
for he thought that, chalilah, his hope was lost
of ever being able to repair this damage.
For he knew that the essence of teshuvah
must be from the depth of the heart,
"until He Who knows all hidden things testifies about him
that he will never return to this sin."
So what gain was there in his teshuvah now,
since he no longer ruled over his own soul,
and the yetzer hara would surely entice him again
and he would not prevail against it?
This is why he lamented over himself
before the One Who knows all hidden things,
that if the yetzer hara would entice him
he would be unable to overcome it
and so, chalilah, his hope was lost.
that Kayin's teshuvah had been accepted,
even though it was only lip service —
as they said in the Midrash (ibid.)
that he went out like one who deceives the Mind on High,
for his teshuvah was only outward,
"and I will be a wanderer and a vagrant"
and nevertheless he obtained a compromise:
"And such is the power of teshuvah!" —
that is not from the depth of the heart at all,
for his evil heart is still within him
and he thinks he is deceiving Hashem Yisbarach with his mouth,
even this helps to be accepted.
"A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day:
it is good to give thanks to Hashem" —
even with the admissions of his mouth alone.
And in this light one can understand
כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים קוֹרְאִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִתְשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵּי
"All the prophets call Yisrael to teshuvah, etc.,
and they do not teach what to say";
for it is beyond a person's mind
that he could bend his heart to good,
and taught them with what to appease Him:
That is, the first thing desired of a person
is only that he confess with his mouth,
"They beguiled Him with their mouth," etc.,
where it is stated in the Midrash
that it was only lip service
when they said "We will do and we will hear":
at Sinai they acted with their mouths,
while in the days of Achashveirosh
it was in the heart and not in the mouth,
all the more so when a person
wants to return as his mouth declares,
only that he does not rule over his heart.
that we pray to Hashem Yisbarach
that we merit His accepting our teshuvah completely,
so that the sin is erased altogether,
and not like Kayin, who obtained a compromise
withholding from him only half the decree,
because it was only lip service.
And through what will we merit this?
"May My teaching drop like the rain"
"My teaching shall be pleasant as the rain";
to make our hearts truly good,
"and we will render for bulls the offering of our lips."
And as is known from the reasoning of the Rambam
even though it is under duress:
because in truth every Jewish soul,
in the innermost point of his heart,
wishes to fulfill the mitzvos of Hashem Yisbarach;
only the leaven in the dough holds him back.
and he says it with his mouth as well,
then his mouth and his heart become one.
This is "and we will render for bulls the offering of our lips":
just as in rendering the fruit of the offerings
mere words of the lips are effective,
even though it comes through compulsion,
all the more so with the confession of our lips
which comes from our own good will.
With this the reason is understood
why for the nations teshuvah does not help
that is, to repair the past;
it helps only for the future,
to hold back the decree from them,
that He had spoken to do to them"
And this is because their teshuvah
כִּי נְקוּדַּת לִבָּם הוּא מֵעוֹמֶק רַע;
for the innermost point of their heart is from a depth of evil;
which is not so with Yisrael,
מְגַלֶּה אֶת עוֹמֶק מַצְפּוּן לִבּוֹ לְטוֹב
reveals the hidden depth of his heart to be good,
that the nations are "close to teshuvah":
because they have no sense of this,
that teshuvah must be from the depth of the heart;
rather, with the speech of his lips alone
he is like one who deceives and tricks the Mind on High,
and therefore it is easy for him.
Not so the Children of Yisrael,
who do not wish to deceive their Creator
with the mouth and not the heart;
rather they want to return in truth,
that a gentile who rests on Shabbos is liable to death
for the essence of the holiness of Shabbos
is that all of the past
of the six days of work be repaired,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good," etc.,
"and He rested on the seventh day
And among the nations this power is not found,
to repair the past, as mentioned above.
And this is what they said in the Midrash cited above:
he said "A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day";
for this is the very essence of the holiness of Shabbos,
to repair the past, as mentioned above.
First, "it is good to give thanks,"
and afterwards "to sing praise to Your Name, O Most High":
beyond his own grasp and strength,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב, ב; קִדּוּשִׁין ל, ב)
that a person's yetzer overpowers him,
וְאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וְכוּלֵּי:
and were it not that HaKadosh Baruch Hu helps him, etc.
He further said in the haftarah:
"I say, mere words of the lips —
it takes counsel and might for war"
That is, words of the lips alone
to give oneself, and might and strength.
So too in the war against the yetzer,
for might is in the heart,
"whose heart is like the heart of a lion"
in words of Torah and wisdom
on how to escape its enticements.
when we take the counsel of Ashur
for the war against the yetzer,
rather, we must know in ourselves
that we do not have this strength on our own.
"We will not ride upon a horse" —
this is the matter of alacrity in action,
as they said in Perek Arvei Pesachim
six things were said about the horse:
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
So too they said of David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
that he would doze like a horse
and so they said of the level of the Avos,
that they "ran before Me like horses"
And he said that we should not rely
on the strength of one's alacrity
in the service of Hashem Yisbarach,
לְהִנָּצֵל עַל יְדֵי זֶה מֵהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
to be saved thereby from the yetzer hara;
for on this too we have nothing to lean upon,
"nor will we any longer say 'our god'
to the work of our hands";
only on His mercies, may He be blessed,
that He will purify our hearts,
"for in You the orphan finds mercy" —
meaning one who knows in his soul
that he has no strength at all of his own,
"He encourages the orphan and the widow"
that first they become like unintentional sins,
"like one with a blemish who has been healed";
and after this, "I will love them freely."
And consequently, as water reflects face to face,
from the heart's own free will,
they will be turned into merits.
וְהִנֵּה מָצִינוּ בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Now we find that David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
in this very matter of his sin:
except to confess with his mouth,
But as for the teshuvah being
from the depth of the heart,
the sin would be wiped away entirely,
for this he asked of Hashem Yisbarach:
"Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your kindness;
according to Your abundant mercy, erase my transgressions"
And on this the parable is brought
to one who had a great wound;
and was astonished at his great wound,
that healing it would cost a great fortune;
and the sick man answered him,
יֵשׁ לִי מְעַט מָעוֹת לְשַׁלֵּם לְךָ,
"I have a few coins to pay you,
and the rest, do for me out of your kindness."
I have no power in my hand
except that I know my transgressions.
who came to heal a sick man's wound;
he said to him, "I am grieved for you,
that you have a very great wound."
He replied, "What does it matter to you?
Is it not for your sake,
so that you will take a large fee?"
in order to teach teshuvah to the individual.
that it is about this that the pasuk says,
"so that You are justified when You speak," etc.
It is as we find with Adam HaRishon,
that before Creation it was written,
only He came to hang the pretext
So too with David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
He wished to find a pretext
to make him liable to death;
was fit to be alive and enduring,
וְעַל זֶה אִיכְתַּב לֵיהּ דָּבָר זֶה,
and for this reason this matter was written of him;
and this is "Against You alone," etc.,
And he said, "Behold, You desire truth in the inward parts,
and in the hidden part make me know wisdom"
that is, in the hidden place
make me know from the aspect of chochmah.
"Purge me with hyssop and I will be pure"
hyssop alludes to one's own lowliness,
as Chazal said regarding the metzora
let him lower himself like hyssop;
And he said, "Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow"
they will become white as snow"
but here he said "whiter than snow,"
which is to refine still further,
and this is the aspect of Mashiach,
which is the life of the World to Come,
And in truth, fit for this
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זַ״ל (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כה, א):
David, King of Yisrael, lives and endures";
only, because the time was not yet
therefore there was hung on him
And as we find in the Gemara (Yoma 86a):
that is, relative to his lofty soul,
Therefore the clarification of this was not achieved
בְּחַיָּיו שֶׁל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
in the lifetime of David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
but only in the days of his son Shlomo,
"At that moment David came to life."
"Hide Your face from my sins," etc.
as it is stated in the Midrash (Midrash Tehillim 19:16)
like the parable of this Kusi:
And this is "Hide Your face from my sins":
from before His face, may He be blessed.
that this is the meaning of the verse
"And he will say on that day," etc.,
"and I will surely hide My face," etc.
the Face comes to be hidden from the sins.
And not as the Ramban wrote
who explains that this "and he will say"
and this does not seem right,
the saying is in the heart,
as in "And Haman said in his heart," etc.
"From where do we know that speech is like action?
'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made'"
that the sin be erased entirely.
"Create in me a pure heart, O God"
so that he is like a new creation;
and this is when it is like merits.
"and renew a steadfast spirit within me"
that he should have ruach hakodesh.
And this is "Restore to me the joy of Your salvation,
and let a generous spirit sustain me"
this is when it will be even
